newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firmer after seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firmer after seesaw trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei stock index futures ended modestly firmer on Friday, tracking the Japanese stock market which posted small gains in late action.
Prices seesawed around the previous day's close but eased toward the critical 19,000 level before short covering came in to lift the market above opening levels.
"If the cash market can regain some momentum to close above 19,750 a few times, it would look more promising for futures," a European commission house dealer said.
The key March Nikkei contract closed at 19,395, up slightly from Thursday's close of 19,285.
The cash Nikkei 225 average settled 77.46 points higher at 19,369.04, but fears for further weakness prevailed.
Foreign investors in Japanese stocks were thought likely to liquidate yen-based assets due to Japan's sputtering economic recovery, with the yen weakening recently against the dollar.
"Interest rates will definitely stay at historical lows which ought to push the yen lower again," one currency trader said, noting the Nikkei 225 was dampening yen demand.
The Nikkei, still in a defensive posture, was likely to test the midpoint of a technical trend at 18,520 points next week.
